setup.baseline: Advanced New Game wizard in the supplied executable.
setup.variable: One universe setting at a time.

procedure: Create a new advanced game with fixed settings and record every field range and default.
Generate one universe for each size and record planet count, span and opponent count.
For each density, record planet counts across at least three seeds/settings.
For each player-position option, record the resulting home-world placement and the minimum starting separation between players.
Toggle clumping and compare nearest-neighbor distances.
Record the effect of every advanced checkbox and player-slot type.
Verify the year 2400 start and common home-world inventory in a generated game.

documented: Sizes: Tiny 400 ly, Small 800, Medium 1200, Large 1600, Huge 2000 (documented-only).
Normal density is about one planet per 5,000 ly^2; Sparse about one per 6,500; Dense about one per 4,000; Packed adds 30% over Dense except in Huge (documented-only).

Advanced options include Beginner: Maximum Minerals, Slower Tech Advances, Accelerated BBS Play, No Random Events, Computer Players Form Alliances, Public Player Scores and Galaxy Clumping (documented-only).
Player slots support predefined/custom/computer/no player, and difficulty affects opponent count and skill (documented-only).
All games start in year 2400; home worlds share a common starting inventory (documented-only).

unresolved: Exact planet-count distributions and clumping geometry are unknown.
Whether Packed is identical to Dense in Huge is documented but unverified.
The command-line game.def ranges are documented-only.
notes: PR6 implements the generation arithmetic from stars-decompile/create.c (a later 2.60j RC3 build), not from stars26i.exe. The help/decompilation Packed-count difference and the designed RNG mapping are documented in docs/rules/universe-generation.md; this scenario remains documented-only.
